plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag: a mid-level long hold separates positive-gain with inertia from dead-zone/no-response and gives first slope and curvature for settling time.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y should rise monotonically from ~0.17 after a short lag/delay, with positive slope that gradually flattens as heat loss grows, ending clearly above start but well below soft limit.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests H4 decay at u=0: measures self-cooling rate, time constant and ambient equilibrium, plus noise at falling/s settled conditions; also lowers y to enable safe future mid-level holds to pin down gain/linearity and u to hold 0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: If H4 heat-loss hypothesis is right, y should decay monotonically from ~0.53 toward ~0.17 with gradually flattening negative slope (exponential-like, tau order 100-200 s), crossing the 0.5 target band downward, plus sensor wiggle ~+/-0.01 with occasional larger downward dips as in E1.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests steady-state gain linearity and u needed to hold 0.5 with a second amplitude below 0.4; settling slope at this level distinguishes linear gain from saturation and directly informs controller feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If heater-gain plus heat-loss hypotheses are right, y should rise from ~0.17 toward ~0.45-0.52 with gradually flattening positive slope, entering or approaching the 0.475-0.525 band late in the hold but staying well below 0.85, with +/-0.01 wiggle and possible brief downward spikes as in E1/E2.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Second-amplitude steady-state gain and feedforward u to hold 0.5: distinguishes linear gain (~0.35 holds 0.5) from saturation/sublinearity and is required to set controller bias without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain plus heat-loss hypotheses are right, y should rise from ~0.19 toward ~0.44-0.50 with gradually flattening positive slope, approaching but not fully settling in 360 s, staying well below 0.6, with baseline wiggle ~+/-0.02 plus occasional brief negative dips up to ~0.06 as in E1/E2.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain and feedforward u to hold 0.5 plus settling confirmation: extending the same 0.3 hold toward full settling (total ~540 s, ~3 tau) distinguishes true equilibrium ~0.52 from saturation/drift and directly sets controller bias.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain plus heat-loss hypotheses are right, y should stay near 0.46-0.54 and drift slowly upward from ~0.48 toward ~0.52 with flattening slope, remaining in/near the 0.475-0.525 band much of the time but with +/-0.02 wiggle plus possible brief negative dips up to ~0.06, staying well below 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Local incremental gain and time constant just below the operating point (0.3->0.2 step) needed to set feedback trim without overshoot/oscillation; distinguishes linear ~1.1 gain (~0.11 drop) from saturation and pins tau near target.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H2/H4/H5 are right, y should decay gradually from ~0.51 toward ~0.39-0.42 with steepest negative slope first (~-0.0005 to -0.001/s) then flattening, dropping below the 0.475 band lower edge within ~50-100 s, staying well below 0.6 and above 0.3, with +/-0.02 wiggle plus occasional brief negative dips up to ~0.06 as in E1/E2/E4/E5; last-5s slope still negative, confirming tau ~150-200 s and not yet settled.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Local incremental gain and falling time-constant just below the operating point (0.3->0.2 step) needed to set feedback trim without overshoot; distinguishes linear ~1.1 gain (~0.11 drop) from saturation and pins tau near target.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H2/H4/H5 are right, y should fall gradually from ~0.53 toward ~0.39 with steepest negative slope first (~-0.0008/s) then flattening, reaching ~0.43-0.46 after 200 s with last-5s slope still negative, staying >0.35 and well below 0.6, with +/-0.02 wiggle plus occasional brief negative dips up to ~0.06 as in E1/E2/E4/E5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Second settled steady-state level and falling time constant near operating point to confirm linear gain ~1.1 and set feedforward bias and feedback trim without offset or overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H2/H4/H5 are right, y should continue falling gradually from ~0.46 toward ~0.39-0.42 with steepest negative slope early (~-0.001/s) then flattening toward ~0 by end of 300 s (500 s total at u=0.2), staying >0.35 and well below 0.6, with +/-0.02 wiggle plus occasional brief negative dips up to ~0.06 as in E1/E2/E4/E5/E7.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases y (positive steady-state gain): sustained u=0.3-0.4 drives y up by >0.3, u=0 lets it fall from ~0.54 to ~0.19, and stepping 0.3->0.2 drives y down 0.53->0.46 in 200 s.

Response has inertia with time-constant ~150-250 s and settling ~450-600 s with negligible pure delay: E1 still rising at 250 s (slope 0.0013), E4 still rising at 360 s (slope 0.0033), extended 0.3 hold to ~540 s total in E5 reaches slope ~0.0003, and E7 still falling after 200 s at 0.2 (slope -0.001).
No large dead-zone: u=0.3 and u=0.4 both produce sustained positive slope and >0.3 rise from ambient, and u=0.2 produces sustained negative slope from ~0.5.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient ~0.15-0.20 due to heat loss; E2 decayed from 0.544 to mean 0.175 over 480 s.

Steady-state y is approx linear in u with gain ~1.1 above ambient (Ss ~0.17+1.1*u), so u to hold 0.5 is ~0.28-0.30; E5 settles at ~0.505 at u=0.3, E1 at 0.4 extrapolates to ~0.61, and E7 fall 0.531->0.462 in 200 s toward ~0.39 is consistent but not yet settled so second settled level still needed.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to 0.05 band.

Sensor has baseline variation ~+/-0.02 plus intermittent large negative dropouts ~0.05-0.07 large relative to band and requiring filtering/robust control; seen in E1,E2,E4,E5 dip to 0.455, and E7 dip to 0.419.
